frequency_question: How often do jurisdictions with an active CCyB framework raise the buffer rate from zero during a non-crisis economic expansion window?
membership_rule: Includes any jurisdiction that established a structural CCyB framework post-2016 and operated it through economic cycles, excluding emergency pandemic-related reductions or ad-hoc non-framework capital measures.

cases.name: Norway Norges Bank CCyB increase to 2.5%
UK FPC CCyB post-pandemic restoration to 2%
US Federal Reserve CCyB active framework period at 0%

provenance_note: claims 30 cases from only 6 named (5.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 30 observed distinct national tightening cycles; 8 direct upward adjustments from 0% or lower baseline states.
known_gaps: Varying domestic mandate structures mean some central banks separate macroprudential authority from monetary policy.
skeleton: Active regulatory jurisdictions with CCyB frameworks (approx 10 major jurisdictions) observed over rolling 3-year windows across the post-Basel III implementation era.
multiplier: 10 jurisdictions times 3 distinct macroprudential tightening phases yields approximately 30 comparable decision opportunities, with roughly 8 recorded hikes above 0%.
validity_reason: Macroprudential frameworks and Basel III institutional behaviors evolve slowly over multi-year structural cycles.
